problem_statement: LangChain's streaming layer contains a cluster of distinct but interrelated defects across its sync and async execution paths that collectively cause crashes, silent data loss, missing metadata, and spurious warnings in production deployments. First, an SSE format mismatch between non-standard proxies (such as the AWS Bedrock Anthropic proxy) and the Anthropic SDK causes streaming to fail entirely, producing zero chunks with no actionable error. Second, the disable_streaming="tool_calling" flag crashes with an AttributeError in async streaming mode because _default_params unconditionally forces stream=True, and the flag's suppression logic is over-broad — incorrectly disabling streaming for all conversation turns whenever any tools are bound, not just tool-calling turns. Third, the agent factory's async execution path uses ainvoke instead of astream, silently preventing on_llm_new_token callbacks from firing; LangGraph's use_astream=True does not propagate down to model-level token streaming, meaning callers who depend on streaming callbacks receive no tokens without any error signal. Fourth, the structured-output streaming path emits Pydantic serializer warnings because it serializes chunks using a bare model_dump() call, inconsistent with the already-corrected non-streaming path. Fifth, HTTP response headers — including x-request-id and other provider correlation identifiers — are dropped from response_metadata when using with_structured_output(..., method="json_schema").stream(), making distributed tracing and provider-side debugging impossible. Finally, a test covering the empty-stream error callback case carries an incorrect assertion masked by an xfail marker, meaning the regression coverage for this scenario is illusory. Together these defects erode confidence in streaming as a reliable, observable, and debuggable execution mode across LangChain's supported model integrations.
target_user: LangChain library users and integration developers who rely on streaming — including developers building real-time LLM-powered applications with async agents, structured-output pipelines, tool-calling workflows, and non-standard model proxies such as AWS Bedrock

acceptance_criteria.given: LangChain is configured to use an AWS Bedrock Anthropic-compatible proxy
acceptance_criteria.when: a streaming call is made and the proxy returns SSE events in its native format
acceptance_criteria.then: at least one chunk is received by the caller and no format-mismatch or zero-chunk failure is raised

acceptance_criteria.given: a model has tools bound and disable_streaming="tool_calling" is set
acceptance_criteria.when: an async streaming call is initiated
acceptance_criteria.then: the call completes without an AttributeError and streaming is active on non-tool-calling turns while suppressed only on tool-calling turns

acceptance_criteria.given: an async agent is executed via the agent factory with a registered on_llm_new_token callback
acceptance_criteria.when: the model produces tokens during async execution
acceptance_criteria.then: on_llm_new_token is called at least once per streamed response, confirming astream is used instead of ainvoke in the async path

acceptance_criteria.given: LangGraph's use_astream=True is set and a model is invoked asynchronously
acceptance_criteria.then: on_llm_new_token callbacks fire at the model level, confirming the flag propagates to model-level token streaming

acceptance_criteria.given: a chain using with_structured_output in streaming mode processes a response
acceptance_criteria.when: output chunks are serialized and yielded
acceptance_criteria.then: no Pydantic serializer warnings are emitted to stderr or the logging system

acceptance_criteria.given: a request is made using with_structured_output(..., method="json_schema").stream()
acceptance_criteria.then: response_metadata on the streamed output contains the x-request-id header value returned by the provider

acceptance_criteria.given: a streaming call produces an empty stream triggering the error callback
acceptance_criteria.when: the test_stream_error_callback test runs without the xfail marker
acceptance_criteria.then: the assertion passes with the correct expected value and the test is green

acceptance_criteria.given: any of the above fixes are applied
acceptance_criteria.when: the full streaming test suite is executed
acceptance_criteria.then: no previously passing tests regress and no new xfail markers are introduced

out_of_scope: Adding streaming support to model integrations that do not currently support it
Redesigning the callback system architecture beyond the async propagation fix
Adding new structured-output methods or JSON schema formats beyond fixing the existing json_schema stream path
Performance optimization of the streaming pipeline (e.g., reducing chunk latency or buffering strategy changes)
Support for non-Anthropic provider proxies beyond the Bedrock SSE fix
End-to-end tracing or observability platform integrations beyond preserving existing response headers in metadata

risks.description: Each of the six pain points has a frequency of 1, meaning the evidence base is thin. It is possible some defects are environment-specific or already partially addressed in recent commits, making prioritization difficult without broader user signal.

Fixing the disable_streaming="tool_calling" suppression logic requires changing turn-level streaming control behavior; the new scoped suppression may interact unexpectedly with multi-turn or parallel tool-calling patterns not covered by existing tests.

Replacing ainvoke with astream in the agent factory async path is a behavioral change; any caller relying on the current (broken) non-streaming behavior as a side effect — e.g., expecting a single complete response object — may see regressions.

The SSE format fix for Bedrock proxy compatibility may require maintaining a compatibility shim that diverges from the canonical Anthropic SDK stream format, creating a long-term maintenance burden if the SDK evolves its SSE contract.

Preserving HTTP response headers through the structured-output streaming path may require threading header data through multiple abstraction layers; if those layers do not expose headers today, the fix scope may be significantly larger than a targeted patch.
